title: Lesson 2: BLESS - Begin in Prayer
description: God blessed Abram so that he would be a blessing to every family on earth, and that blessing has reached you. Every BLESS rhythm begins with prayer: talk to God about your one before you talk to your one about God.

blocks.text: In Lesson 1 you wrote the names on your map and asked, Who's your one? Now you will learn to love your one with the BLESS rhythms: Begin with prayer, Listen, Eat, Serve, and Story. They are not a program. They are simple habits that turn the places where you already live, work, and play into places of mission. Every one of them starts with a promise God made thousands of years ago.

blocks.alt: BLESS - Begin with Prayer, Listen, Eat, Serve, Story

blocks.title: Blessed to Be a Blessing
blocks.text:
Long before there was a church, a Bible, or a single follower of Jesus, God spoke to a man named Abram. He was seventy-five years old, living in Haran with his wife Sarai, and they had no children. God told him to leave everything familiar: "Go from your country and your kindred and your father's house to the land that I will show you" (Genesis 12:1).

Then God made him a promise that would shape the rest of the Bible: "I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you and make your name great, so that you will be a blessing... and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed" (Genesis 12:2-3).

Abram had nothing to offer God. No land, no children, no great name. God simply chose to bless him, and the blessing came with a purpose. "So Abram went, as the LORD had told him" (Genesis 12:4).

Notice the order. God blessed Abram before Abram did anything, and the blessing was never meant to stop with him. It was meant to flow through him to every family on earth. That promise has reached all the way to you. Paul says God "preached the gospel beforehand to Abraham", and "those who are of faith are blessed along with Abraham" (Galatians 3:8-9). If you belong to Jesus, you are part of that blessing. You are blessed to be a blessing.
2.1 - Who did God use to bless you on your way to Jesus?
Jesus Prays for You First

Every BLESS rhythm starts with something Jesus has already done for you, and prayer comes first. On the night Peter would deny Him, Jesus told him, "I have prayed for you that your faith may not fail. And when you have turned again, strengthen your brothers" (Luke 22:32). Jesus has not stopped. He "always lives to make intercession" for His people (Hebrews 7:25). Before you ever pray for your one, Jesus is praying for you.
Abraham Prayed for His Neighbors

Years after that first promise, Abraham learned that judgment was coming on Sodom, the city where his nephew Lot lived. He did not shrug, and he did not gloat. He "still stood before the LORD" and pleaded for the city, again and again: What if there are fifty righteous people there? Forty-five? Thirty? Ten? (Genesis 18:22-32). The man God had blessed spent that blessing praying for his neighbors.

That is the first BLESS rhythm. Talk to God about people before you talk to people about God. Mission is God's work before it is yours. Long before you noticed your one, God already knew their name, their story, and what keeps them up at night. Prayer is how you find out where He is working and join Him there. It is also how He changes your eyes, so the people you have walked past start to look like people He loves.

First of all, then, I urge that supplications, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings be made for all people... This is good, and it is pleasing in the sight of God our Savior, who desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
2.2 - Write your one and two to four other names from your map who do not yet follow Jesus, with one thing you know about each.
Your Prayer Card
Here is a simple way to pray for your one, and for each name on your card, with more than a quick "bless them." Pray three things for each person.

blocks.title: Their Life, Their Heart, My Part
content: Their life. Pray for what they are carrying right now: health, family, work, money, a hard decision. Pray the way you would want a friend to pray for you.
Their heart. Pray that God would draw them to Himself and open their eyes to Jesus. Only He can do that (John 6:44), so ask Him boldly.
My part. Pray that God would open a door, give you eyes to notice it, and give you the courage and kindness to walk through it.

blocks.text: Carry it in one phrase: their life, their heart, my part. It is simple enough to sketch on a napkin, and it keeps your prayers personal and centered on the gospel.

Make this one habit, not a second system. Open the Daily Prayers app in your Growing Apps, the prayers you built from the Lord's Prayer pattern in 101, and add your one and your other names to the Pray for people to know Jesus section. That is your kingdom step. Each day, when you pray "Your kingdom come," pray their life, their heart, and your part for each name. If you have not built your daily prayers yet, this is a good week to start.

blocks.title: Your Daily Prayers
blocks.description: Add your one and your other names to the Pray for people to know Jesus section of your Daily Prayers app, so praying for them becomes part of the Lord's Prayer pattern you already use.

blocks.text: Making Prayer a Habit

Prayer for neighbors grows best when it is tied to something you already do. Pray for your one while the coffee brews, on your commute, or when you pull into the driveway. Some people take a prayer walk, quietly praying for each home they pass or each desk at work. You do not need a quiet hour. You need a few honest minutes, most days.

Prayer also happens in the middle of life. You can pray a short, silent prayer in the middle of a conversation: Lord, help me listen. Give me the right words. Sometimes the simplest open door is a question for your one: "How can I pray for you?" If it feels natural, pray with them right then in a sentence or two. Then write it down and ask about it next week. Few things say "I care" like remembering.
Continue steadfastly in prayer, being watchful in it with thanksgiving. At the same time, pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to declare the mystery of Christ.
2.3 - When and where in your day will you pray for your names, and what will remind you?
Prayer Is Not a Performance

You might read this and remember every time you said "I'll pray for you" and then forgot. Take heart. Prayer is not a test you pass to stay in God's good graces. You come to the Father because Jesus has already made the way, and He is still praying for you. When you miss a day, do not quit. Just begin again.
Over time, prayer leads into the rest of BLESS. The person you pray for becomes the person you listen to, eat with, serve, and in time share your story with.
2.4 - For each name from 2.2, which next step feels most natural: listen, share a meal, serve, or share your story?
This Week's Practice
Pray for your one by name every day this week: their life, their heart, my part. Add your other names as you can. Then look for one natural moment to ask your one, "How can I pray for you?"
Lesson 2 Review

God blessed Abram so that through him all the families of the earth would be blessed, and in Jesus that blessing has reached you. You are blessed to be a blessing, and the blessing begins with prayer. Jesus prays for you first. Then, like Abraham, you talk to God about people before you talk to people about God. Pray most days for your one and the other names on your card, their life, their heart, and your part, and watch for the doors only God can open.
In the next lesson, you will learn the next two rhythms, Listen and Eat, and how an open table can turn your one into a friend.
Closing Reflections
What is one key thing you learned from this lesson?
What is one step you are going to take this week?
What is a prayer request for this week?
